dimensions.assessment: Directly applies to visiting government representatives and armed forces members from Taiwan, as well as relevant U.S. departments managing official communications and ceremonies.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense shall permit members of the Armed Forces and representatives from Taiwan... to display... the flag of Taiwan

dimensions.assessment: Represents a symbolic and protocol-oriented change regarding the display of flags and insignia during specific official events and communications.
dimensions.evidence: The purposes referred to in subsection (a) are--(1) the wearing of official uniforms; (2) conducting ceremonies or functions; and (3) appearances on Department of State and Department of Defense social media accounts

dimensions.assessment: Contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or economic revenue changes.
Modifies protocol rules for the Department of State and Department of Defense regarding foreign symbols, explicitly maintaining the broader One China Policy.
dimensions.evidence: Nothing in this Act shall be construed as a change to the One China Policy of the United States

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a permanent statutory authorization governing official protocol and displays.

missing_information: Any potential diplomatic or geopolitical fallout or administrative costs of updating protocol guidelines.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill permits visiting dignitaries and service members from Taiwan to display the flag of Taiwan and military insignia during official uniforms, ceremonies, and Department of State and Defense social media appearances.
